thread:
Ken (Customer): Hey team, after we moved our inference traffic through an SSH->SOCKS5 hop to our corp egress gateway, calls to Redwood intermittently fail. We see TLS handshake failures and 401s even though the same token works from a laptop outside the network. No rate-limit headers.
Claire (Support): Sorry you're hitting this, Ken. Can you share a minimal repro and a couple of logs? curl -v output and a short tcpdump would help.
Ken (Customer): Repro steps:
1) From app host (no direct internet): export https_proxy=socks5h://127.0.0.1:1080
2) curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://inference.redwood.com/v1/generate --data '{"prompt":"hi"}'
Output sometimes: "SSL: no alternative certificate subject name matches target host name 'inference.redwood.com'" or sometimes 401 JSON {"error":"unauthorized"}.
Claire (Support): Thanks — two different failures suggest either TLS is being terminated/rewritten by the proxy or the Authorization header is lost/changed midstream. @Ajay any immediate checks?
Ajay (SRE): Quick checks:
- DNS: run `dig +short @<corporate-dns> inference.redwood.com` and `dig +short @1.1.1.1 inference.redwood.com` to confirm both resolve the same IP.
- TLS from inside: `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername inference.redwood.com -showcerts` (use the IP you got) to inspect cert chain and subjectAltName. If proxy is MITMing TLS, you'll see the proxy's CA.
- header preservation: `curl -v --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:1080 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://inference.redwood.com/ -o /dev/null` and check the proxy logs for the outgoing request. Many corporate proxies drop Authorization unless CONNECT passthrough is enabled.
Ken (Customer): Ran dig — corp DNS returns the gateway IP (10.10.0.5) while public DNS returns a public LB IP. openssl to public IP (1.2.3.4) shows Redwood cert ok; openssl to 10.10.0.5 shows corporate cert signed by our corp-CA.
Marisol (Eng): That confirms a TLS-inspecting proxy rewriting certs. Two important behaviors we see with customers:
1) If the proxy terminates TLS and re-encrypts (MITM), it must present a cert that includes inference.redwood.com in SAN to the client OR clients must trust the proxy's CA. Otherwise you get SAN mismatch.
2) If the proxy rewrites or removes Authorization, our gateway sees no token -> 401 and the request is discarded.
Ajay (SRE): Short-term workarounds:
- For SDK services: configure egress NAT/direct outbound for hosts that call Redwood (bypass proxy).
- PAC file change: add `!inference.redwood.com` to bypass rules so CONNECT goes direct.
- If bypass not allowed, ask infra team to enable CONNECT/TLS passthrough for inference.redwood.com:443 so proxy doesn't terminate TLS.
Claire (Support): Diagnostic commands you can paste here (redact tokens):
- `curl -v --socks5-hostname 127.0.0.1:1080 https://inference.redwood.com/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" --trace-ascii /tmp/curl.trace`
- `tcpdump -nni any host inference.redwood.com and port 443 -w /tmp/redwood.pcap`
- `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername inference.redwood.com -showcerts`
Ken (Customer): We ran curl trace — I can see CONNECT to gateway then GET to 1.2.3.4 with a different cert subject. Also saw proxy sending `Proxy-Authorization` to the gateway but no Authorization header on the upstream request.
Marisol (Eng): That matches header-stripping. If the Authorization is being removed at proxy, the gateway will 401. Two options: have the proxy forward the `Authorization` header (not typical for forward proxies) or have it allow raw CONNECT so the TLS tunnel is opaque.
Ajay (SRE): Additional things to ask your infra team:
- Add inference.redwood.com to proxy bypass list OR allow CONNECT to port 443 without TLS termination.
- If corporate CA must MITM, install the corp CA into the trust store of the app runtime (system or container) so `openssl s_client` validation and SDK trust succeed.
- Ensure proxy doesn't rewrite Host/SNI, and if using SOCKS5, use `socks5h` (hostname resolution via proxy) vs `socks5` which resolves locally.
Ken (Customer): If we add the corp CA to the container image trust store, is that safe? Will it impact anything on Redwood side?
Marisol (Eng): From our side nothing changes — we only care that the client trusts the cert presented. Adding corp CA to your runtime will stop SAN mismatch errors. However, Authorization header removal is still a functional problem; you'd still get 401s unless CONNECT is used.
Claire (Support): Final recommended path:
1) Patch PAC / egress rules to bypass inference.redwood.com (preferred).
2) If bypass not possible, request TLS passthrough for that FQDN on the proxy.
3) As a fallback, add corp CA to trust store (to fix TLS errors) but also ask proxy team to preserve Authorization header or forward Proxy-Authorization correctly.
Ken (Customer): I'll open a ticket with infra to add the bypass and request CONNECT passthrough. I'll attach the curl trace and the tcpdump. Thanks.
Ajay (SRE): One more small check for you before closing: after bypassing, verify `curl -v https://inference.redwood.com/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>"` from the app host resolves and returns 200. If you still see intermittent 502/timeout, paste tcpdump and we'll look at routing/NAT.
SRE-Bot: Reminder: when you paste pcap, please scrub any PII and only attach artifacts needed for debugging. :lock:
Ken (Customer): Will do, thanks everyone :thumbsup:
